function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times. Here’s a quick overview of the key figures who helped turn it into a scientific discipline:

| Person | Contribution |
|--------|--------------|
| **Thales of Miletus (c. 600 BCE)** | First recorded observations of static electricity (rubber rubbed with fur). |
| **William Gilbert (1544‑1603)** | Coined the word *electricus* (from Greek *elektron*, amber) and wrote *De Magnete*, laying the groundwork for electrical science. |
| **Benjamin Franklin (1706‑1790)** | Conducted the famous kite experiment, proving that lightning is electrical and introduced the concepts of positive/negative charge. |
| **Alessandro Volta (1745‑1827)** | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery), demonstrating that electricity can be generated chemically. |
| **Michael Faraday (1791‑1867)** | Discovered electromagnetic induction, leading to the development of generators and motors. |
| **James Clerk Maxwell (1831‑1879)** | Unified electricity and magnetism into a single set of equations (Maxwell’s equations). |

So while no single “discoverer” exists, the systematic study of electricity began with William Gilbert and was advanced by many scientists over centuries.
